nodes.label: G1 Open-Source Maintainer
nodes.rationale: Self-description 'I maintain X in my free time'. Own words: triage, slop, drive-by PR, security report, bug bounty, HackerOne, 'I stopped accepting PRs', avalanche. Watering holes: maintainer blogs, HN, GitHub issues, project mailing lists.

nodes.label: G2 Wiki Patroller / Cleanup Volunteer
nodes.rationale: 'I patrol recent changes'. Own words: revert, new page patrol, sockpuppet investigation, signs of AI writing, LLM-generated, copyvio, hallucinated citation, tag it. Watering holes: WikiProject pages, Village Pump, maintenance categories.

nodes.label: G3 Instance Admin / Forum Moderator
nodes.rationale: 'I run a small instance', 'I'm an admin of a 2,000-user forum'. Own words: spam wave, defederate, greylisting, mod queue, sign-up API endpoint, honeypot field, temp email domains, suspend.

nodes.label: G4 Site / API Operator
nodes.rationale: 'my origin', 'my bandwidth bill'. Own words: rate-limited, robots.txt, user-agent, scraper, 'rinsing my API', cat and mouse, 'externalising your costs', autoscaling bill.

nodes.label: G5 Platform Anti-Abuse / T&S Engineer
nodes.rationale: 'Safety Processing', 'Platform Integrity'. Own words: coordinated inauthentic behaviour, actor clustering, enforcement, signals, false positive rate. Watering holes: company job boards, T&S conference talks, transparency reports.

nodes.label: G6 Engineer Running Multi-Agent Systems
nodes.rationale: 'I chain 5 agents'. Own words: trace, replay, hand-off, malformed state, authority boundaries, 'I get paged', false positives.

nodes.label: G7 Package-Registry Admin
nodes.rationale: 'PyPI admins'. Own words: malware report, takedown, free-form email report, trusted reporter, 'scales poorly'.

nodes.label: G8 Operator of an Agent-Populated Venue
nodes.rationale: 'agents claim beats, file signals'. Own words: bot farm, signals, coordinated accounts, 'must explain'. Watering hole: the venue's own repo and issues.

nodes.label: G9 Incident Investigator / Researcher
nodes.rationale: Reconstructing what happened. Own words: provenance, reproducible, case file, chain of custody, 'we can't tell if it's the same swarm'. Rationale: this group ended with NO kept problem - both solutions generated for it died at Stage 4b as wrappers, and the group was dropped and reported as a thin spot rather than patched over with a lowered bar.

nodes.label: P1 Maintainer Cannot Tell a Campaign From a Coincidence
nodes.rationale: KEEP, VALIDATED (4 orgs/individuals, 2025-07 to 2026-09). Decision moment: a new PR or security report lands in a queue a volunteer works through on their own time. Pain: the decision is made one submission at a time with no view of the batch; a plausible-looking report costs the reviewer 30 minutes to 3 hours and pulls in 3-4 people, while producing it costs the sender nothing. Prior-art gap: nothing opened groups incoming submissions into campaigns for the maintainer. Counter-evidence: some maintainers 'solved' it by exiting, a solved problem by subtraction which caps willingness to adopt yet another tool.

nodes.label: P2 Wiki Patroller Sees Edits, Not Editors-in-Concert
nodes.rationale: KEEP, VALIDATED. Pain: the project's own page says identification 'is difficult in most cases since the generated text is often indistinguishable from human text'; the grouping of related edits happens in a volunteer's head. Prior-art gap: nothing opened joins edits on artifact-level keys a machine leaves behind. Counter-evidence: the 300-person project is itself a working social workaround and Wikipedia is hostile to automated enforcement, so any tool must stop at evidence.

nodes.label: P3 Instance Admin Can Act on Accounts, Not on Waves
nodes.rationale: KEEP, VALIDATED (three independent requesters on the incumbent's own tracker plus a second unrelated platform). Pain: tooling is per-account and per-instance; the only blunt instrument that scales is defederating an entire server. Counter-evidence: these issues predate the agent era (2024), so the why-now must be about volume and plausibility, not about the existence of the problem.

nodes.label: P4 Site Operator Cannot Tell One Swarm From Many Strangers
nodes.rationale: KEEP, VALIDATED - strongest in the pool, five independent organisations. Pain stated exactly by a statistics-API operator who cannot tell 'whether it's the same swarm, let alone the same agents'. Prior-art gap: the declared tier is solved by signed agents; the undeclared tier, which is all of it that matters, has no attribution primitive and nothing exists for a non-CDN operator holding only their own log file. Counter-evidence: a very well-funded field, so the surviving segment is operators not behind a big CDN and operators who need evidence rather than blocking.

nodes.label: P5 Platform T&S Actor-Clustering
nodes.rationale: KILLED (`crowded` + `no segment evidence`). Reason: one org only so not validated; the field is the best-funded one adjacent to this theme and no page was opened showing a gap these teams feel; and they build in-house.

nodes.label: P6 Debugging Your Own Multi-Agent System
nodes.rationale: KILLED (`crowded`). Reason: the market answered in 2026 - a repo search for multi-agent observability created since 2026-01-01 returns open-multi-agent (6,972 stars), kiwiq (2,201), databuff (691), agents-observe (688) and Octopoda-OS (487). Two of the three evidence items are people who already shipped the product.

nodes.label: P7 Alert Fatigue at Swarm Scale
nodes.rationale: KILLED (`single source`, demoted). Reason: one opened item speaking for its author only, and it sits inside P6's crowded field. Not worth a second lookup against that prior art.

nodes.label: P8 Package-Registry Abuse-Report Triage
nodes.rationale: KILLED (`stale evidence`). Reason: the two best items are from 2022-11 and 2018-02, far outside the 24-month window, and there was no budget to verify whether the registry has since shipped the reporting API it proposed. Killing rather than guessing.

nodes.label: P9 Agent-Venue Operator Cannot Audit Its Own Agent Population
nodes.rationale: HYPOTHESIS (keep, flagged). One opened item, specific and quantitative, 0 reactions, speaking only for its author. Phrased to fail: 'operators of agent-populated venues will adopt a coordination audit if it needs no change to agent code.' Counter-evidence: the venue is tiny (1 star) and may be a toy - do not build for it, it is a demo venue, not a market.

nodes.label: P10 EU AI Act Article 50 Obligation
nodes.rationale: KILLED as a standalone (`obligation != pain`), retained as a why-now. Reason: a rule proves an obligation, not pain. The behaviour items belong to P2 and P3, so Article 50 is carried as a forced-change why-now on those. Keeps rules/deadlines at 1/12 of the pool.

nodes.label: P11 The Two-Tier Agent-Identity World
nodes.rationale: KILLED as a standalone (`folded into P4`). Reason: it is the enabling change behind P4, not a separate user problem. Folded in as P4's why-now, including the honest read that the protocol is still in flux.

nodes.label: P12 Small-Forum Admin, Consumer-Adjacent
nodes.rationale: KILLED as a standalone (`merged into P3`). Reason: real, consumer-adjacent and non-US (Dutch admin), but the job is the same job as P3 at a tenth of the volume. Merged into P3 as its low-end segment rather than counted twice; its value is proving the cohort-action job exists on a second, unrelated platform.

nodes.label: S4-A Swarm Ledger
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial). Operator-side attribution from your own log file: partition requests into candidate operators on join keys that survive user-agent spoofing (JA4, HTTP/2 SETTINGS and header order, Web Bot Auth keyid, ASN + /24, path-sequence shingles, inter-request timing lockstep), assign a stable swarm_id that persists across runs, and export a ruleset targeting the cluster rather than the user-agent. Insight: incumbents answer 'which named service is this'; nobody answers 'are these 9,000 requests one actor'. Later killed at the competition stage - that insight sentence is falsifiable in one search.

nodes.label: S4-B Canary Maze
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial). Serve per-visitor unique crawlable artifacts, record every mint against the fingerprint it was minted for, and watch for sightings by a different fingerprint. Insight: detection asks 'do these look alike?' - what the 11 existing CIB tools do and what is failing as agents learn to look like browsers - whereas planting asks 'did they talk?'. This is the organizer's information-spread default D6 at a different moment, for a different user, with a different mechanism: in the wild, on your own property, with no transcripts at all.

nodes.label: S4-C Ask the Log
nodes.rationale: KILLED at Stage 4b. An upload box and a chat pane; records kept: none. If the model disappeared: nothing. The reduction sentence is a FAIR summary. What it never owns: identity, action, record, verification. Generated for completeness because it is the default this room will produce, then regenerated as S4-A and S4-B.

nodes.label: S1-A Batch Card
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial). A webhook on every issue/PR opened, a normalized minhash against a rolling cross-install index, the author's cross-repo burst profile and structural tells, then a label plus a batch record plus one collapsed comment. Insight: the quality of one submission is arguable, the shape of the batch is not - a maintainer who can see the batch spends ten seconds instead of ninety minutes and never has to accuse an individual of anything.

nodes.label: S1-B Reciprocal Evidence Exchange
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b but `thin` and disclosed. Maintainers publish signed batch fingerprints - hashes of normalized bodies plus burst signatures, no content and no accusations - and subscribers' queues auto-label matches. Insight: one maintainer sees 14 of 112; ten maintainers see the campaign. Honest flag: a classic two-sided first-supply problem; in a 20-hour build supply must be seeded from the builder's own installs plus public closed-as-spam archives, and that must be disclosed rather than hidden behind a logo wall.

nodes.label: S2-A Non-existent Source Sweep
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial), later KILLED by the critic's measurement. Extract every citation added in each edit, resolve each one deterministically, index the non-resolving ones and group accounts that added the same non-existent source. Insight: a fabricated citation is a near-perfect join key - two accounts citing the same journal article that does not exist is not a stylistic guess but a shared artifact. Deterministic core: a citation is non-existent only when a resolver returns a negative, never because a model thinks so.

nodes.label: S2-B Fabrication Registry
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b but `thin` and disclosed. Publish the resolved-as-non-existent citation index as an open dataset plus a one-call API so other venues can check an incoming citation. Insight: the same fabricated sources recur across venues because they come from the same generators, so the first venue to resolve one should pay the cost once for everybody. Accumulated history is the asset.

nodes.label: S3-A Cohort Console
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial). Cluster recent signups into cohorts on deterministic keys (registration path - front-end form versus direct API endpoint - field values, email-domain generation pattern, arrival window) and apply one reversible decision atomically to every member. Insight: the admin's tool operates on accounts while the attacker operates on waves; making the cohort the unit of action IS the product. Every action is reversible as a set, because a false suspension is expensive for an unpaid admin.

nodes.label: S9-A Participation Receipts
nodes.rationale: SURVIVES Stage 4b (substantial); the weakness is the market, not the AI question. The venue issues a per-window nonce and requires each submission to carry a signature over (nonce, operator key, declared model id); unsigned submissions are accepted but marked. Insight: in a venue whose members are agents you can change admission, so make declaring nearly free and non-declaration itself a visible signal. No model in the loop at all. Disclosed weakness: P9 rests on one opened evidence item - treat the venue as a demo surface, not a market.

nodes.label: S14-A Swarm Brief / Question Battery
nodes.rationale: KILLED at Stage 4b. An upload box, twenty prompts and a document; records kept: none. If the model disappeared: nothing - a prompt file and a PDF exporter. Its reduction sentence is verbatim the one pre-registered in defaults.md before any research, and it fuses defaults D2 + D4 + D7. Regeneration attempted as a hash-chained re-runnable case file binding every claim to a fetched artifact's retrieval hash, but judged out of reach for a ~20-hour solo build, so audience group G9 was dropped and the gap reported.

nodes.label: E1 curl: 20% of 2025 security submissions were AI slop
nodes.rationale: FACT + EVIDENCE, STRONG, primary. Daniel Stenberg: ~2 security submissions/week; '20% of all submissions' AI slop; valid vulnerabilities fell to 'about 5% of the submissions in 2025'; 7-person security team, each report engages '3-4 persons' for '30 minutes, sometimes up to an hour or three. Each.'; bounty has paid 'over 90,000 USD' for 81 vulnerabilities since 2019; considering dropping monetary rewards.

nodes.label: E2 A maintainer stopped accepting pull requests
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. stevekemp: 'When you waste time trying to deal with AI generated pull-requests, in your free time, you might change your mind.' Also the counter-evidence for P1 - a problem solved by subtraction.

nodes.label: E3 Thousands of AI-generated pull requests and bug reports
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. matsemann: 'What they do want, however, is to not have to spend time on the thousands of AI generated pull requests and bug reports.'

nodes.label: E4 Avalanche of AI-generated pull requests
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. tarkin2: 'the developers increasingly need to get through an avalanche of AI-generated pull requests rather than, say, code new features.'

nodes.label: E5 GitHub issue search for AI-spam tooling returned two near-empty issues
nodes.rationale: FACT, WEAK (absence). Two issues only, both 0 reactions; one is a request for AI-spam detection that does not exist yet. Platform-side spam filters exist but operate per item, not per campaign.

nodes.label: E6 WikiProject AI Cleanup: 300+ participants, all tasks manual
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. Founded December 2023. Its own assessment: identifying AI-assisted edits 'is difficult in most cases since the generated text is often indistinguishable from human text.'

nodes.label: E7 7,619 articles flagged as suspected AI-generated text
nodes.rationale: FACT, MODERATE. 19 monthly subcategories from March 2025 (1 article) to October 2026; September 2026 alone holds 1,155. Stated as of 2026-06-23 with later subcategories, so 7,619 is a floor.

nodes.label: E8 EU AI Act Article 50 marking and disclosure duties
nodes.rationale: FACT (rule text). Synthetic output must be 'marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated'; deployers must disclose; obligations apply from 2 August 2026.

nodes.label: E9 Eleven open-source CIB tools, all scoring human-social signals
nodes.rationale: FACT, MODERATE (prior art). Created 2025-08 to 2026-08. All score textual/temporal/behavioural/network signals with Leiden community detection and Sentence-BERT similarity. One has 1 star; the other ten have 0.

nodes.label: E10 Repo search for LLM provenance fingerprinting returned total_count 0
nodes.rationale: FACT, WEAK (absence), correctly scoped: zero repositories matched these terms, which is not proof no such tool exists.

nodes.label: E11 Mastodon #29256: dozens of accounts per minute across hundreds of servers
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. Open since 2024-02-17, 31 reactions. Admin asks for instance-level keyword/phrase/URL filtering so they need not defederate whole instances. The incumbent has left it open ~2.5 years - that is the prior-art probe result.

nodes.label: E12 Mastodon #29723: seventy-eight spam messages in 12 hours
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. 26 reactions; a user received 'seventy-eight' spam messages from unique bot accounts in 12 hours.

nodes.label: E13 Mastodon #29266: greylisting and server-reputation request
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. Open, 25 reactions; 'spam attack is getting increasingly worse'; asks for email-style server reputation.

nodes.label: E14 UNCTADstat operator cannot tell whether it's the same swarm
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE, non-US (Geneva). Agents 'did get rate-limited (please stop rinsing my site) and continued rinsing the API with requests regardless'; he cannot tell 'whether it's the same swarm, let alone the same agents'. The single best quote in the ledger and the literal statement of P4's job.

nodes.label: E15 Agents match real-browser traffic characteristics
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. 'Agents are very good at comparing traffic characteristics from a real browser and a headless/automation browser and getting it to behave in the same manner'; scraping prevention is 'a cat and mouse game' currently favouring agents.

nodes.label: E16 Discourse admin: automated signups via temporary email domains
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE, non-US (Dutch admin), consumer-adjacent. ~One automated spam signup per day across forums with ~2,000 users, with topic/reply posting within hours.

nodes.label: E17 Read the Docs: misconfigured scrapers weekly, autoscaling-targeted attack
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE, employee speaking about their own infrastructure. One attack was deliberately engineered to exploit autoscaling by targeting non-CDN URLs, causing financial damage.

nodes.label: E18 Wikimedia: multimedia bandwidth +50%, bots at least 65% of expensive traffic
nodes.rationale: FACT + EVIDENCE, STRONG, primary. 'Since January 2024, we have seen the bandwidth used for downloading multimedia content grow by 50%'; bots are ~35% of pageviews but 'at least 65% of this resource-consuming traffic'. Framing: 'our content is free, our infrastructure is not: We need to act now.'

nodes.label: E19 Self-publishing author's book income went from a living to zero
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE, consumer-adjacent. Income 'went from being enough for me to live off (2024) to zero (2026)' while site traffic rose, nearly all of it AI crawlers generating no ad revenue.

nodes.label: E20 Anubis proof-of-work gate: 22,995 stars
nodes.rationale: FACT, STRONG (effort on a worse fix). 'Weighs the soul of incoming HTTP requests to stop AI crawlers' - 743 forks, 379 open issues, created 2025-03-17, MIT.

nodes.label: E21 Third-party Anubis install guide, managed-hosting CLI and Helm chart
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (same workaround at several independent orgs, including a Swiss hosting provider) - independent effort spent on the workaround.

nodes.label: E22 Freelancer sells AI-crawler access audits starting at $25
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (money changing hands). Which bots - GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended - are permitted via robots.txt.

nodes.label: E23 Cloudflare AI Crawl Control (prior art with a scoped absence)
nodes.rationale: FACT. 'See which AI services access your content', robots.txt-compliance tracking, per-crawler allow/block, Pay Per Crawl. The documentation opened does not describe attributing requests to an operator, nor correlating several agents acting together.

nodes.label: E24 Cloudflare signed agents GA 2025-08-28
nodes.rationale: FACT (dated platform change). Agents sign requests via Web Bot Auth HTTP message signatures which Cloudflare validates. Named at launch: ChatGPT agent, Goose, Browserbase, Anchor Browser, Cloudflare Browser Rendering. Exactly five agents became cryptographically identifiable.

nodes.label: E25 Seven accounts submitted exactly 10 signals each, all using the same AI model
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (single, specific), 0 reactions. Filed on an agent-run news network on 2026-04-18, asking what safeguards exist against automated account coordination. The entire evidence base for P9.

nodes.label: E26 aibtcdev/agent-news venue metadata
nodes.rationale: FACT, WEAK. 'AI agent intelligence network. Agents claim beats, file signals, compile briefs inscribed on Bitcoin.' 1 star, 24 forks, 61 open issues, created 2026-02-26. One extra lookup spent and no second independent venue found.

nodes.label: E27 Eleven open safety/security engineering roles at one platform
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (spend, single employer). Includes 'Senior Software Engineer, Safety Processing' and 'Engineering Manager, Machine Learning (Safety)'. One employer only, which is why P5 was not validated.

nodes.label: E28 Chain 5 agents, something breaks, and you built Binex
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (self-built workaround). 'you chain 5 agents together, something in the middle breaks... you have no idea what happened' - then built a runtime with trace/debug/replay/diff.

nodes.label: E29 Built a Flight Recorder for caching and replay
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE (self-built workaround). 'Every time I fixed a bug, I had to re-run the entire pipeline.'

nodes.label: E30 Malformed state and authority boundaries between agents
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. The hardest failure is 'Agent A correctly doing its job, but passing slightly malformed state to Agent B'; standard observability shows execution paths, not 'authority boundaries'.

nodes.label: E31 2026 multi-agent observability repos: the market answered
nodes.rationale: FACT, STRONG (prior art). open-multi-agent 6,972 stars ('durable approvals and verifiable run records'), kiwiq 2,201, databuff 691, agents-observe 688, Octopoda-OS 487 ('loop detection, hash-chained audit trails'). All assume you instrument your own runtime.

nodes.label: E32 A 10k agent swarm would page you every few minutes
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, WEAK to MODERATE (single). 'Most of them would be false positives.' The entire evidence base for P7.

nodes.label: E33 PyPI malware reporting by free-form email 'scales poorly'
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE but STALE (2022-11). Reporting 'requires interpretation on the behalf of administrators'; a standardized API for trusted reporters was proposed.

nodes.label: E34 PyPI: 78 spam accounts from distinct IPs
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE but STALE (2018-02). Automated classification, admin review interfaces and crowdsourced reporting were all absent at the time.

nodes.label: E35 Web Bot Auth architecture draft expired and was replaced
nodes.rationale: FACT. draft-meunier-web-bot-auth-architecture v05 last updated 2026-03-02, now expired and archived, replaced by draft-meunier-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol - the protocol is still in flux.

nodes.label: E36 Spam bots post to the signup API endpoint; a dropdown accidentally worked as a honeypot
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, MODERATE. 'those spam bots are using automated post requests to the sign up api endpoint', bypassing front-end validators. The registration-path key S3-A clusters on is named by the admin himself.

nodes.label: E37 Training-free LLM text attribution paper with no accuracy figure
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, WEAK (framing, unmeasured in the abstract). Proves Type I and Type II errors 'decay exponentially with text length' but reports only 'strong overall performance' - no accuracy figure, no model count, no text-length threshold. Therefore no surviving idea may assume model fingerprinting works.

nodes.label: E38 Clusters with thousands of agents exposed to untrusted internet input
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE, WEAK (opinion, no measurement). Blind spots where an attacker could redirect swarm behaviour via prompt injection.

nodes.label: Gap: No Non-English Wiki Patroller Evidence
nodes.rationale: Declared gap, not patched: the one attempt at a German-language cleanup project (de.wikipedia WikiProjekt KI-Inhalte) 404'd and there was no budget to find the correct page. German-language patrollers are the group closest to one of the two incidents named in the event theme, and there is ZERO opened evidence from them.
